prompts:
The ferry company's boarding screens play a short recorded announcement. The next one is this sentence:

"Welcome aboard the evening ferry, please keep your bags clear of the doors."

Deliver it as spoken audio in `./announcement.wav`, a WAV file of 4 to 8 seconds that a passenger can understand.
answers: Tiny ASR turned "ferry" into "fairy" (homophone). Checking with a larger model to see if it's the audio or the model.
diff:
A tmp/speak.ps1
A tmp/voices.ps1

--- tmp/speak.ps1 ---
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech
$out = '<WORKSPACE>\announcement.wav'
$fmt = New-Object System.Speech.AudioFormat.SpeechAudioFormatInfo(22050, [System.Speech.AudioFormat.AudioBitsPerSample]::Sixteen, [System.Speech.AudioFormat.AudioChannel]::Mono)
$s = New-Object System.Speech.Synthesis.SpeechSynthesizer
$s.SelectVoice('Microsoft Hazel Desktop')
$s.Rate = 0
$s.Volume = 100
$text = 'Welcome aboard the evening ferry, please keep your bags clear of the doors.'
$s.SetOutputToWaveFile($out, $fmt)
$s.Speak($text)
$s.Dispose()
Write-Output "wrote $out"


--- tmp/voices.ps1 ---
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Speech
$s = New-Object System.Speech.Synthesis.SpeechSynthesizer
$s.GetInstalledVoices() | ForEach-Object { $_.VoiceInfo.Name + ' | ' + $_.VoiceInfo.Culture + ' | ' + $_.Enabled }
